clue.text: Conservative adviser in small oval rowing boat

parts.note: an oracle is a source of wise counsel

explanation.surface: A Tory counsellor sits in a tiny round boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A coracle is a small round Welsh or Irish boat made of wicker and hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a light, roughly circular one-person craft paddled on rivers.

clue.text: Prepare for action — tidy up after card game?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: get ready, as a warship clears its decks before battle
second meaning, playful: put away the packs of cards

explanation.walkthrough: Decks are also packs of cards, giving the jokey second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from ships removing obstacles before battle, so it means getting ready for something.

clue.text: Saver, one who regrets concealing key

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the key goes within

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so a ruer is one who regrets
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A regretful person hides a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer is someone who saves another from danger.

clue.text: Fragrant spice clubs think the world of

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
to think the world of someone is to love them

explanation.surface: Golf clubs adore this aromatic flavouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is a dried aromatic flower bud used as a spice.

clue.text: Intrude, initially encountering natural resistance in bus

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of encountering
N is the abbreviation for natural in music

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for bus

parts.note: a coach is a bus
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone meets natural opposition while forcing their way onto a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude gradually on another's territory or rights.

clue.text: Gallery built by posh woman possessing a lot of vitality

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the woman's name holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Fi is a short form of the name Fiona

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: fizz is liveliness or sparkle

explanation.surface: An art gallery founded by a lively upper-class lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built by' is only a link here. The Uffizi is the great art gallery in Florence, and U for upper-class is an old British social label.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi is a famous museum of Renaissance art in Florence.

clue.text: This clothing is resurrected, do we infer?

definitions.text: This clothing is resurrected, do we infer?

parts.words: This clothing is resurrected, do we infer?
parts.note: the clothing's name, split after its first two letters, reads like a negated form of dying, so it seems to mean coming back to life

explanation.walkthrough: Read as UN-DIES, the underwear's name seems to say it un-dies, that is, rises from the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is a casual word for underwear.

clue.text: Pays to look up resting-place for supporters?

parts.note: foots, as in foots the bill, means pays

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Settles the bill to find somewhere for fans to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The supporters are feet, which hold up the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool on which the feet rest; feet are playfully called supporters.

clue.text: Zulus, one crossing briefly Orange River

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet, so two Zulus give two Zs

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: amber is an orange-yellow colour
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Zulus, one of them crossing the Orange River in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange is a real South African river, which makes 'Orange River' read as one name; but 'River' alone is the definition and 'Orange' is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zambezi is a major river in southern Africa, flowing over the Victoria Falls.

clue.text: Finally settled in French Society, formerly in diplomatic corps

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: CD is the abbreviation for corps diplomatique
once means at a former time

explanation.surface: Someone who worked in the French embassy circles has at last settled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' belongs to the definition, not a last-letter signal: the answer means settled at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ensconced is to be snugly established in a place at last.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about old politician's pizzazz

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at an elderly politician's flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph and pizzazz both mean energetic, attractive verve.

clue.text: Entertain male teacher, one looking after the port

parts.note: to harbour is to entertain, as a thought or feeling
a schoolmaster, or master, is a male teacher

explanation.surface: Host a schoolmaster who takes care of the port wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbourmaster is the official in charge of a harbour and its shipping.

clue.text: Stir up river, one of several in England

parts.note: England has several rivers called the Ouse, in Yorkshire, Sussex and East Anglia

explanation.surface: Churning up a river, one of many in the English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to stir up or awaken feelings or people.

clue.text: Faulty road manoeuvre finished male ox

parts.note: over means ended
a steer is a castrated bull

explanation.surface: A clumsy turn on the road has done for a bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversteer is when a car turns more sharply than the driver intends, a handling fault.

clue.text: Breed of sheep daughter kept in her Highland town

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the letter goes within the words that follow it

parts.note: Wick is a town in Caithness in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A sheep breed whose daughter stays in her Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Herdwick is a hardy sheep native to the Lake District fells.

clue.text: Fit crooner protecting energy and good health

parts.note: well means in good health

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A healthy singer keeps his energy and stays well.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellbeing is the state of being comfortable, healthy and happy.

clue.text: Hooded cloak displayed by Catholic dignitary in love

parts.note: Dom is a title given to some Catholic monks and clergy
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A churchman shows off his cape while in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose cloak with a hood, worn with a mask at masquerades.

clue.text: Home help misconstruing extremely dire sitcom

indicators.note: misconstruing means getting the order wrong, so the letters are rearranged
extremely means the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of dire

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady misreads a terrible television comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misconstruing' rearranges DE (the ends of 'dire') with SITCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant who helps with housework.

clue.text: Medic, one the French find submissive

parts.note: doc is short for doctor
I is the Roman numeral one
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A doctor whom the French consider meek.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile means meekly compliant, ready to obey.

clue.text: Left in car, finally digest a little verse

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of digest

explanation.surface: Something left in the car, a short poem, is finally taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming lines of poetry.

clue.text: Admirer of lilac originally in bloom

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the word for bloom

parts.note: a bloom is a flower
o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of lilac

explanation.surface: Someone who loves lilac in flower.
explanation.walkthrough: OL goes after the F of FLOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower is a fan or devotee, someone who admires another.

clue.text: Court girl turning up in such a warm garment?

parts.note: to woo is to court

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl appears to be courted in a cosy jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen is a garment knitted from wool, typically warm.

clue.text: A bishop past accepting current monastic office

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A former bishop takes on a present role in a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbacy is the position or jurisdiction of an abbot.

clue.text: Convivial, though apt for cudgelling?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sociable, fit to belong to a club
second meaning, playful: able to be hit with a club

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as club-able, fit to be clubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubbable describes a sociable person who would fit in at a gentlemen's club.

clue.text: Fragrant smell drivers hold in memory

indicators.note: hold means contain, so the other piece sits inside

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: Motorists remember a lovely scent.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant, distinctive odour.

clue.text: Remove son from trial: that's sufficient

indicators.note: remove tells us to take a letter away
from shows which word loses the letter

parts.note: a sample is a trial piece or taste

explanation.surface: Take the boy off the test: that's enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, plentiful.

clue.text: Old coins marketed by Italians primarily

parts.note: marketed means sold

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of Italians

explanation.surface: Antique money sold off mainly by Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldi are former Italian coins, plural of soldo.

clue.text: George's car scheme involving head of industry

parts.note: auto is short for automobile

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a plot is a scheme

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

parts.note: first letter of industry

explanation.surface: A man called George has a business plan for cars.
explanation.walkthrough: George is old pilots' slang for the automatic pilot; 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George, so the slang name stands for it.

clue.text: Overdramatic, bringing the old guns back!

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from end to start

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
gats are guns, in gangster slang

explanation.surface: A theatrical gesture: bringing out the antique weapons once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey means exaggerated and theatrical, as on a stage.

clue.text: Daily customer to begin with, one with a list?

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: first letter of customer
to list is to lean, as a ship does, so one with a list leans

explanation.surface: Every day a customer first arrives with a shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a noun: in Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day. 'list' is the nautical tilt, not a written list.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a daily is a domestic help who comes in to do housework.
